newsitem.title: USA: Augat sees no impact from SEC probe.
newsitem.headline: Augat sees no impact from SEC probe.

text.p: Augat Inc chief financial officer Gordon Bitter said the company expects no material impact on its business from a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission investigation of the company's accounting policies.
"We don't think it's a big deal. We're cooperating fully with the commission on this," Bitter told Reuters in an interview.
Shares in the Mansfield, Mass.-based maker of electromechanical components were off 1/4 to 27.
Bitter said the investigation was disclosed by the company in its 10Q filing with the SEC.
He said the agency is looking into accounting practices including "revenue recognition under certain complex contracts, inventory reserves, how we do backlog accounting."
Augat has provided data to the SEC and discussed the investigation with the agency, but Bitter said he could not project when the inquiry might be concluded.
"At this stage, it does not appear to be anything material," he said.

Augat said in early October it reached a definitive agreement to be acquired by electrical components maker Thomas & Betts Corp, of Memphis, Tenn., in a stock transaction valued at about $550 million.
"We've kept Thomas & Betts apprised. They're certainly aware of it," Bitter said.
He said the acquisition is "moving along very nicely."
Shareholders are expected to meet December 11 "to formally ratify the transaction."
